profile.name: Mohammad-Hossein Namdar
profile.title: PhD Student in Astrophysics
profile.subtitle: Cosmology, gravity, and the formation of cosmic structure
profile.short_bio: I study how cosmic structure forms and evolves, with a focus on dark-sector cosmology, nonlinear gravity, halo statistics, and computational methods that connect theory with data.
profile.long_bio: I am a PhD student in Astrophysics at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile and a research assistant at the Centro de Astro-Ingeniería UC. My work sits at the intersection of theoretical cosmology, numerical computation, and data analysis. I am particularly interested in late-time dark-sector models, the nonlinear growth of structure, halo statistics, modified gravity, and optimal-transport methods in cosmology.
profile.availability: Open to research collaborations and scientific discussions.

research.title: Matter-Diffusion Cosmology
research.summary: Cosmological constraints on constant and nonlinear matter-diffusion models using contemporary late-time data.
research.details: This project studies a family of interacting dark-sector cosmologies in which matter undergoes velocity diffusion and exchanges energy with an effective scalar-field dark-energy component. We implement the constant model and four evolving diffusion parametrizations in SimpleMC, validate their background evolution, and compare them with ΛCDM and CPL using supernovae, BAO, and cosmic-chronometer measurements.

research.title: Interacting Dark Energy
research.summary: Exploring interacting dark-energy and dark-sector extensions with physically motivated energy exchange and cosmological constraints.
research.details: Together with Alireza Zafari, I am developing interacting-dark-energy scenarios and studying how dark-sector energy exchange modifies the expansion history and observable cosmological signatures. The work complements the matter-diffusion programme while keeping the model assumptions and observational interpretation distinct.

research.title: Monge–Ampère Gravity & Structure Formation
research.summary: Analytical and computational study of structure formation under an effective Monge–Ampère gravitational law.
research.details: My work on Monge–Ampère gravity includes the weak-field Poisson limit, spherical solutions, linear and nonlinear spherical collapse, Eulerian perturbation theory, one-loop matter power spectra, and halo statistics. The broader goal is to understand how nonlinear, optimal-transport-inspired gravity changes cosmic-web morphology and clustering relative to the Newtonian case.

research.title: Computational Cosmology at UC
research.summary: Research in computational astrophysics and cosmology at the Centro de Astro-Ingeniería UC.
research.details: As a PhD student and research assistant at UC Chile, I work within a computational research environment on problems connected to cosmology, astrophysical structure, simulation, and scientific data analysis. This programme includes ongoing collaboration with Prof. Rolando Dünner and Prof. Gaspar Galaz; project-specific public details will be added as the work matures.
